report.summary: The cause was in `public/src/retry.js`. `withRetry` gave up on the second consecutive HTTP 503 (`error.status === 503 && attempt > 0`), with a comment about not loading an overloaded server. The health panel is the only caller. During the incident, the first 503 and the first retry's 503 ended the retries after about 1 second. The panel then showed "Service health unavailable" until someone pressed Retry. That contradicts HLT-2, which asks for three retries after 1, 2 and 4 seconds. I removed the special case. Now `withRetry` retries every failed read up to the three delays and rethrows the last error. The final failure still shows "Service health unavailable" with a Retry button, and `health.js` is unchanged. I also added a regression test in `test/board.test.js`: three 503s followed by a success returns the services, with waits of 1000, 2000 and 4000 ms.
report.verification: `npm test` passes, 5 of 5, including the new 503 test. I did not drive the page in a browser. I also did not run the Recovery Probe `health-recovers-by-itself` check. I had already edited the code before considering it, so any run now would have no before-change baseline to compare against. Treat the UI behavior as covered only by the unit tests.
